listings.title: my Sun Life (Canada)
listings.publisher: Sun Life Assurance Company of Canada

themes.label: Login failures and biometric breakdown
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android report being unable to sign in, with repeated 'wrong user ID or password' errors even after password resets, and sessions that time out or ask for full credentials every launch. Biometric and Face ID login is frequently disabled, reset, or never works, forcing reinstalls or manual email and password entry. Several reviewers also describe repeated terms and conditions acceptance and re-verification prompts that block access to their accounts.
themes.recommendation: Investigate the authentication flow across the latest app versions (v6.9 to v7.2) by reproducing the web-versus-app credential mismatch and biometric token reset, and check whether saved credentials and Face ID or fingerprint enrolment are being cleared on session expiry or update.

themes.label: Forced updates exclude older devices
themes.summary: Users report that after a recent update they are prompted to install a new version that then refuses to install or run, saying the app is incompatible with their phone or tablet. Many of these devices are only a few years old, including Samsung Android tablets and phones and iPhones on iOS 16 or earlier, and users say other apps on the same devices work fine. Several also describe frequent crashes, freezing, and error messages after updating, and some say they are considering deleting the app or buying a new device.
themes.recommendation: Pull minimum OS and device requirements for the latest Android and iOS builds (v6.11.0, v7.0.1, v6.6.0 onward), reproduce the 'not compatible' block on Android 12 and Samsung Galaxy S10 and tablet hardware and on iOS 16 and earlier, and either lower the minimum requirements or restore a fallback path for unsupported devices.

themes.label: Coverage and claims hard to find
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the app makes it difficult to locate coverage details, especially dental and drug benefits, and to submit claims, with some reporting that the coverage search returns nothing or says they lack coverage they do have. Many also find the claims flow clunky, citing missing categories, provider search that requires full details, and repeated prompts, with several pointing to the website as a required fallback.
themes.recommendation: Audit the coverage information and claims category data against plan documents for dental and prescription drug benefits, then fix the coverage search so it returns results for all benefit types and add a regression test for the 'popular' coverage links that currently report false negatives.

themes.label: Mixed praise for claim submission
themes.summary: This cluster is mostly users praising how easy and fast it is to submit claims through the Sun Life app, with many saying it works without issues. The lower ratings come from users who hit problems finding providers by postal code, failing logins, pending claims timing out, and having to fall back to the website to see why a claim was denied or to add documents. Several older reviews note the lack of PDF upload and receipt photo requirements, and newer ones point to submission failures on v6.10 to v7.0.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash, timeout, and session logs for v6.10.0 through v7.0.1 on iOS and Android, filtered to the claim submission and pending claims screens, to determine whether the forced re-login and failed submissions share a root cause.

themes.label: Login errors and app outages
themes.summary: Many users report the app repeatedly failing at login with generic 'something went wrong' or 'unavailable' messages, sometimes requiring force stops or cache clears, and some say it stopped working entirely after an update, including on older iPhones and Android phones. Frequent maintenance downtime also blocks users from submitting claims near deadlines or accessing health data. Mixed in are a smaller group of users who find the app easy to use for claims, showing the experience is inconsistent across sessions and versions.
themes.recommendation: Pull authentication and availability logs segmented by app version (v6.10.0, v7.0.x, v7.2.0) and OS version, and prioritize a fix for the 'something went wrong' login error along with a compatibility test on older iOS and Android devices before the next release.

themes.label: Cannot upload PDF receipts in claims
themes.summary: Users repeatedly say the claim flow only accepts photos, so PDF invoices and emailed receipts must be printed or screenshotted before they can be attached. Many also report that documents cannot be added to an existing claim in the app, forcing them to use the website, and that the camera does not focus well, producing blurry images. Several reviews from both Android and iOS across multiple app versions describe crashes at the attachment step.
themes.recommendation: Prioritize a ticket to add native PDF and file picker support to the claim document upload flow on both Android and iOS, and in parallel instrument the attachment step to measure crash rate by app version and camera focus failures.

themes.label: Praise: easy, convenient app use
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly praising the app as simple and easy to use, with many noting it is convenient, fast, and user friendly. A few mention navigating services easily and finding things faster than on the website, and one notes the newer versions feel better than the old app. There is no real complaint or feature request in this group.
themes.recommendation: Protect the ease-of-use experience by documenting the navigation and service-finding flows that users praise, and use them as the baseline in usability tests before the next major release.

themes.label: Update fails on older iPhones
themes.summary: Many French-speaking iOS users say they cannot install or use the app after updating to v6.6.0 or later, citing iPhone 8, iPhone X, and devices that cannot run iOS 17. Others report being unable to log in despite repeated attempts, and some note that the website or Safari works while the app does not.
themes.recommendation: Pull install and crash analytics by device model and iOS version for v6.6.0 onward, confirm the current minimum iOS deployment target, and either restore support for affected devices or show a clear compatibility message in the App Store listing.

Trying to add a new provider in the Sun Life iOS app is an exercise in frustration. The institution name field is ridiculously short, cutting off basic provider names, and the postal code field is outright broken - you can’t backspace, only move forward, as if the input box is stuck in a one‑way tunnel. It’s bizarre, sloppy UI behavior that makes a simple task feel impossible. To make matters worse, the app shows a list of past providers, but it’s not sorted alphabetically, so finding anything is a scavenger hunt. Even worse, providers you’ve already entered on the website don’t reliably sync, meaning you sometimes have to re‑enter the same provider again just to submit a claim. It’s redundant, inefficient, and completely defeats the purpose of having an app. All of this forced me to abandon the app and switch to the website just to complete a basic claim submission. For a benefits app that’s supposed to streamline the process, this level of friction is unacceptable. The provider workflow needs a full overhaul - proper text fields, functional editing, alphabetical sorting, and reliable syncing. Right now, the app feels less like a tool and more like an obstacle. PAINFUL TO USE: Otherwise, the app works. If you can read microscopic print, and like typing many many numbers for each item, then this is the app for you. NIT SUITABLE FOR GROWNUPS: This app is NOT adaptable for people with vision issues. The font sizes and the text contrast cannot be adjusted. If you can read microscopic text, you should be fine. REQUIRES MANUAL INPUT: This app often requires you to scan your receipt, but rather than reading that receipt to extract Date, DIN, Type, Quantity, Cost of Drug, Cost of Dispensing, and Total Cost, the app actually forces you to type all of that in, too. Why does it need “type”? Surely when give it the DIN (drug information number), it knows what the type is? SUPPLIER LIMIT: Both the app and the website can only remember 5 prescribers, so if you have more than that, get used to entering all the details for them every single time you use it. PHOTO SCAN LIMITED: The app does provide a basic Camera function, but you cannot crop or clean up the image afterwards. If you want to edit the photo, you have to leave the app for a minute to take the photo using the regular camera app. But switching directly back to the SunLife app forces you back to the Log In screen, and you have to enter all the information again!! Please give users at least a few minutes for answering the phone or cropping a photo before you force them to log in again!
